elements.label: Browser mockup window scales up toward the Version Details panel

pattern.description: While the user types the new version name ('May Foreca...'), the whole browser mockup scales up (about 1.23x) and drifts left. This centres the Version Details form so the typed name and access settings become legible.
pattern.why_premium: The zoom is motivated by the action. It lands on the field being typed in sync with the voice-over ('call this new version the May forecast'), and its decelerating energy curve (strong start, smooth settle) reads as an eased push rather than a cut.

build_hint.gsap: Scale the screen-recording layer rather than the stage: gsap.to('.browser-mock', {scale: 1.23, xPercent: -9, yPercent: -6, transformOrigin: '70% 35%', duration: 0.5, ease: 'power3.out'}). Run a typewriter on the Name input in parallel: gsap.to('.name-input', {text: 'May Forecast', duration: 0.6, ease: 'none'}) with the TextPlugin.
build_hint.remotion: const p = spring({frame: frame - start, fps, config: {damping: 200, stiffness: 120}}); set transform: scale(interpolate(p,[0,1],[1,1.23])) translate(...) on the browser layer. Type the name with text.slice(0, Math.floor(interpolate(frame,[start,start+18],[0,len],{extrapolateRight:'clamp'}))).

notes: Conflict to check: camera.move is 'none', but scale is 1.2314 and pan_x is -0.09, and the filmstrip shows the whole browser mock and the blue backdrop curve enlarging. This is effectively a push-in on the mockup layer. It is annotated as the b01 layer scaling up (no camera move is asserted), with ui_camera_push_in as the closest pattern. The cursor only moves with the zoom and is not listed. The OCR boxes on the left are partial text cropped by the zoom.
